summary: Since September 2023, intergenerational art programs in the local community have paired young people with elders to share skills, stories and cultures. Started by retired art teacher Layla Bennett with the 'Canvas Crossroads' workshop, the programs have spread, reduced loneliness, drawn government support, and aim to create permanent spaces and mentorship programs.
one_line: Layla Bennett's Canvas Crossroads sparked community-wide intergenerational art programs that connect youth and elders, ease loneliness, and have won local government backing.
key_facts: Intergenerational art programs have blossomed in the local area since September 2023.
Layla Bennett is a 62-year-old retired art teacher who envisioned a community united by art regardless of age.
By October, Layla Bennett had collaborated with local schools and nursing homes to establish the first intergenerational art workshop, 'Canvas Crossroads'.
Canvas Crossroads began on October 15 and meets every Thursday in the art room at Jefferson Elementary.
The success of Canvas Crossroads led to similar programs in community centers and parks district-wide.
Fifteen-year-old Marcus Johnson taught 75-year-old Martha Wallace to use a digital drawing tablet; Marcus calls it 'reversed schooling'.
Younger participants learn oil painting and watercolor, while elders try digital art, street art and virtual reality.
The 'Generations Gala' on November 23 was a community-wide exhibition of work by participants from different ethnic and cultural backgrounds.
12-year-old Aisha Nguyen and 78-year-old Italian immigrant Giovanni Rossi fused Vietnamese and Italian artistic influences.
80-year-old Helen Brooks found solace in art after losing her husband and said the program gave her 'a new lease on life'.
Local psychologists and sociologists are studying the programs' impact; preliminary observations suggest improved family dynamics between children and grandparents.
Councilman James Becker advocates increased funding and integrating similar models into the city's official community development plans.
Long-term goals include more permanent spaces, sponsoring local youth to pursue art education, and mentorship programs.
The article marks half a year since the first intergenerational art program began.
